_source: Transcribed from notebooks/SymFM_NS_SEIRD_Colab.ipynb. L2_mean=10.0 is the code's saturation/failure sentinel (see eval_model()'s `min(l2, 10.0)`), not a measured error -- it means symbolic equation recovery did not converge at any tested N. Confirmed independently in two separate runs of this notebook (the GitHub-hosted version and a local re-run), both giving ERR=0.0% and L2=10.0 at N=50, 250, and 500. This is why the paper's Table 3 SEIRD column reports 0% equation-recovery rather than an L2 error, and why Section 6 (Discussion/Limitations) states symbolic recovery on SEIRD was not achieved at any tested dimension -- state estimation (see pinnobs_results.json) succeeded independently of this.
_status: SUPERSEDED as the paper's reported SEIRD numbers -- see results/seird_symfm_results.json. This run uses the benchmark's original CHRONOLOGICAL train/val/test split, which diagnostics/seird_split_artifact/ found places the test window in a near-zero-derivative regime that destabilizes the relative-L2 metric regardless of model quality. Kept here as a record of the original run, not deleted, but seird_symfm_results.json (representative split) is what Table 3 now reports.
